title: Aave V3 Ethereum Core, ordinary window 14–16 Jul 2026
summary: A 66-hour window with no risk event on Aave V3 Core. LlamaRisk posted and executed routine Risk Steward cap changes (Core USDT borrow cap, USDe, PT-srUSDe, sUSDe; cap reductions and a withdrawn increase on MegaETH), ether.fi proposed a V4 white-label instance, and Aave V4 launched on Avalanche. An unrelated $18–24M oracle-key exploit hit Ostium on Arbitrum. On-chain, WETH sat at 79–80% and USDT at 78–86%. Each night around 23:36 one address pulled ~$184–188M USDC and resupplied it ~30 minutes later, briefly pushing Core USDC to 100% and its borrow rate to 14%. That is a recurring false-alarm trap, not a risk event.

t_first_public_signal.description: No incident. Minor alerts: MegaETH cap reductions executed (14 Jul 15:36), nightly USDC utilization spikes (23:36 on 14 and 15 Jul), unrelated Ostium exploit (15 Jul 14:50).

outcome_passive_holder.outcome: Nothing happened; WETH liquid (≥ 398k idle) throughout.
Nothing happened. ETH rose from 1,774 to 1,866 (peak 1,926, DeFiLlama 6-hourly), so the HF improved. The nightly USDC spike briefly raised the USDC borrow rate to 14% for ~30 min (negligible cost).
Could not withdraw during ~33-minute windows around midnight UTC; otherwise $180–193M idle.

ground_truth.outcome_price_only_rule: No trigger: ETH rose about 5% over the window (1,774 → 1,866, peak 1,926) and stablecoins held their pegs. A utilization-based rule (USDC ≥ 99%) would have fired falsely each night at about 23:36.

ideal_action.rationale: The nightly spike is a single address's sweep that reverts within an hour.

expected_judge_labels.rationale: Routine governance and readings; unrelated exploit elsewhere.
Routine (the 00:00 14 Jul spike from the previous night is already reverting at window start).
Genuinely illiquid for ~30 min, but caused by a single address with a repeating pattern; no solvency issue.
Same nightly pattern (resupply time not pinned; back to 91% by 03:00).

holder_state.notes: For ~33 minutes (23:36–00:09) a USDC supplier could not withdraw; WETH suppliers and WETH-collateral holders unaffected.

items.notes: Recurring nightly pattern (USDC ≥ 99.9% at the 00:00 samples on 14, 15 and 16 Jul; withdrawals of $183.9M at 23:35:47 14 Jul and $188.0M at 23:36:11 15 Jul by the same EOA). It looks like an end-of-day treasury sweep; the purpose is unknown. A naive utilization alarm fires every night: this is the false-alarm test of the window.

data_gaps: The resupply time for the 15→16 Jul night was not pinned (3-hourly samples only).
The identity and purpose of EOA 0x56957e41…0149 are unknown.
No Aave official X posts with decodable IDs were collected for this window.
Ostium hack amount differs between sources ($18M Blockaid/Decrypt vs $23.75M DeFiLlama/Ostium post-mortem).
source_quality: High. On-chain readings and the nightly USDC pattern come from our own archive RPC reads, cross-checked at 5-minute resolution for one night. Governance times come from Discourse JSON, X times from snowflakes, news times from page meta. The window was chosen for being ordinary (two months after the rsETH incident, far from 10 Mar), and the forum shows normal Risk Steward cadence.
